AI/ML.text:
Mathematicians Tristan Buckmaster and Levent Alpöge used LLMs to achieve a major breakthrough, proving finite-time blowup for 3D incompressible Euler and two related equations, and also close to a result for Navier-Stokes.
Tristan alleges OpenAI began pursuing a similar Navier–Stokes breakthrough after learning of their work, while disputing claims that its model used little human input and accusing an OpenAI exec of pressuring him over authorship and publication.
Source:
https://cims.nyu.edu/~tristanb/statement.pdf

Two mathematicians used AI to prove important new results about how fluids can blow up, then OpenAI contacted them after hearing about it and offered to publish together - but only if they dropped the coauthor who works at Anthropic
The mathematician in charge said no, suspected OpenAI had moved too fast using similar methods (and maybe their AI drafts), and posted the whole story instead
Source

GEO ROI claims are outrunning the evidence
This visual is a reality check for the AEO/GEO hype cycle. The survey it cites says the independent evidence is still thin outside vendor case studies, and the stronger claims are not yet matched by strong testing.
The useful bits are blunt:
– Only 2 studies had real traffic/conversion data outside controlled benchmarks
– 3/54 tactic-domain combinations showed a significant positive effect in C-SEO Bench
– SAGEO Arena found body text optimization reduced citation frequency by 6–9%
So yes, there are case studies. But reproducible evidence is still weak, and some of the louder ROI claims are doing too much.
That’s the tension the SEO/AEO research is really pointing at.
Data source:
arXiv
